name: GIS-B-ME
description: GIS-B-ME (GIS-Based Benchmark for Maintenance of Elevators) is a semi-synthetic benchmark for static elevator maintenance scheduling based on real-world urban building locations and directed road networks. The benchmark covers selected study areas in Beijing, Shanghai, and Chongqing and combines real geographic foundations with controlled generation of maintenance tasks, building functional types, service calendars, time windows, and task capacities. GIS-B-ME v1.0 contains 135 benchmark instances across three cities, three task scales, three spatial patterns, and five random seeds, comprising 72,000 instance-level preventive-maintenance task records. The release includes benchmark instances, road-distance and travel-time matrices, frozen geographic inputs, generation configurations, validation outputs, and independently validated best-known feasible schedules. The benchmark is designed to support reproducible evaluation and comparison of static elevator maintenance scheduling methods. The maintenance tasks and business/service attributes are generated under controlled benchmark rules and do not represent actual elevator asset registries of Beijing, Shanghai, or Chongqing.
